questions.question: The pollen needs to be transferred from the stamen to the stigma. If this transfer of pollen occurs in the same flower, this phenomenon is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**self-pollination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Self-pollination** is the transfer of pollen grains from the **stamen to the stigma** of the same flower or another flower on the same plant.
 
• This process ensures **genetic consistency **and can occur in both monocots and dicots.
 
• It is a form of sexual reproduction in plants but does not promote genetic diversity as cross-pollination does.
 
• Plants that predominantly self-pollinate include wheat, rice, and tomatoes.
 
• Mechanisms such as cleistogamy (flowers that never open) ensure self-pollination in some plant species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cross-pollination**

 
 
• It involves the** transfer of pollen from the stamen of one flower to the stigma of another flower**, often requiring external agents like wind, water, or animals.
 
• Cross-pollination promotes genetic diversity and can lead to hybrid vigor in plants.
 
• Common examples include apples, pumpkins, and many types of flowers.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization**
 
 
• It is the process following pollination where male gametes from pollen grains unite with female gametes (ovules) to form a zygote.
 
• Fertilization results in the formation of seeds and fruit in flowering plants.
 
• It can occur in both self-pollinated and cross-pollinated plants.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• It is an **asexual reproductive process** found in fungi, algae, and some plants like ferns and mosses.
 
• Spores are usually single-celled and can develop into a new organism without the need for fertilization.
 
• Spores are highly resistant to environmental stresses and can remain dormant for extended periods.
 
 
 
• **Stamen and Stigma**
 
 
• The **stamen **is the **male reproductive part** of a flower, consisting of the anther and filament.
 
• The **stigma **is the **female reproductive part** of a flower that receives pollen during pollination.
 
• Both stamen and stigma are essential for sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

questions.question: What is the value of power if a man does 50 J of work in 10 s ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The power (P) is calculated using the formula P=(W)/(t), where W is the work done and t is the time taken.
 
• Given: Work Done(W)= 50 Joules Time Taken(t)= 10 seconds.
 
• Substituting the values, P=(50J)/(10s)=5Watts.
 
• Power is measured in Watts (W), which is equal to one Joule per second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work (W)**

 
 
• Work is defined as the energy transferred to or from an object via the application of force along a displacement.
 
• The SI unit of work is the Joule (J).
 
• Work is calculated as W=F.d.cos(theta ), where F is the force applied, d is the displacement, and θ is the angle between the force and the displacement direction.
 
 
 
• **Time (t)**
 
 
• Time is a measure of the duration of an event.
 
• In the context of power calculation, time is the duration over which the work is done.
 
• The SI unit of time is the second (s).
 
 
 
• **Power (P)**
 
 
• Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
 
• The SI unit of power is the Watt (W), which is equivalent to one Joule per second.
 
• Power can also be calculated using the formula P=V.I in electrical contexts, where V is voltage and I is current.
 
 
 
• **Energy**
 
 
• Energy is the capacity to do work.
 
• It exists in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, chemical, and nuclear energy.
 
• Energy is conserved in all processes; it can neither be created nor destroyed, only converted from one form to another (First Law of Thermodynamics).

questions.question: How are three resistances 3 Ω, 4 Ω, and 6 Ω connected in combination, so that their total resistance will be 13 Ω?

options.text: Does not depend on any combination
3 Ω in series with 6 Ω and 4 Ω in parallel

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All in series**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When resistances are connected in series, the total resistance is the sum of individual resistances.
 
• The formula for total resistance in series is: Rₜₒₜₐₗ=R₁+R₂+R₃.
 
• For resistances of 3Ω, 4Ω, and 6Ω in series, the total resistance is 3 + 4 + 6 = 13Ω.
 
• In a series circuit, the **current flowing through each resistor is the same**.
 
• Resistors in series provide a higher total resistance than any individual resistor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallel Circuit:**

 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the total resistance is less than the smallest resistor in the circuit.
 
• The formula for total resistance in parallel is (1)/(Rₜₒₜₐₗ₎=(1)/(R₁)+(1)/(R₂)+(1)/(R₃).
 
• Parallel circuits are used to reduce the overall resistance and to provide the same voltage across all components.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that V=IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in understanding the behavior of electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistors:**
 
 
• Resistors are used to control current flow in circuits.
 
• They are essential in setting voltage levels and for timing applications in electronic devices.

questions.question: Two trains 135 m and 155 m in length, respectively, are running in opposite directions, one at the rate of 80 km/h and the other at the rate of 65 km/h. In how much time will they be completely clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of Train 1 = 135 m

Length of Train 2 = 155 m

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2

Total Distance = 135 m + 155 m = 290 m

Relative Speed = Speed of Train 1 + Speed of Train 2

Relative Speed = 80 km/h + 65 km/h = 145 km/h 

Convert Relative Speed to m/s:

Relative Speed = 145 × 5/18 = 40.28 m/s

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

Time = 290 / 40.28 = 7.2 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Which of the following reactions is an example of decomposition reaction?

options.text: Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight
Formation of water from H₂(g) and O₂(g)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **decomposition reaction **is a type of chemical reaction where one compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• The reaction for silver chloride (AgCl) decomposing in sunlight can be represented as: **2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl2(g**).
 
• This reaction is characterized by the breakdown of silver chloride into silver and chlorine gas.
 
• **Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight due to the formation of metallic silver,** which is grey in color.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reaction**

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more elements or new compounds.
 
• Decomposition reactions often require an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity.
 
• Examples include the **electrolysis of water and thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate**.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition**
 
 
• It is a type of decomposition reaction where a compound is broken down into simpler substances by **heating**.
 
• Example: **Calcium carbonate decomposes into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide when heated**.
 
 
 
• **Photochemical Reaction**
 
 
• These reactions are initiated by the absorption of light.
 
• An example is the **decomposition of silver chloride in sunlight**.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reaction**
 
 
• Redox reactions involve the **transfer of electrons between two species**.
 
• These reactions include both oxidation and reduction processes.

questions.question: Anu is two years older than Kanu, who is twice as old as Tanu. If the total of their ages is 32, then what is the difference in age of Anu and Tanu?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Anu is two years older than Kanu, who is twice as old as Tanu.

**Formula used:**

Let Tanu's age be T years.

Kanu's age = 2T years

Anu's age = 2T + 2 years

Total age = T + 2T + 2T + 2 = 32

**Calculation:**

T + 2T + 2T + 2 = 32

⇒ 5T + 2 = 32

⇒ 5T = 30

⇒ T = 30/5 = 6

Anu's age = 2T + 2 = 2 × 6 + 2 = 12 + 2 = 14

Tanu's age = T = 6

Difference in age = 14 - 6 = 8 years

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Which body part in the human body is composed of stratified squamous epithelium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Stratified squamous epithelium** is a type of epithelial tissue that consists of multiple layers of flat cells.
 
• The primary function of this tissue is to provide **protection** against mechanical stress, dehydration, and microbial invasion.
 
• The outermost layer of the skin, known as the **epidermis**, is composed of stratified squamous epithelium.
 
• These cells in the skin are **keratinized**, meaning they contain keratin, a protein that helps in waterproofing and providing strength.
 
• Stratified squamous epithelium is also found in other parts of the body, such as the **oesophagus and oral cavity**, but the skin's epidermis is the most prominent example.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epithelial Tissue**

 
 
• Epithelial tissues are one of the four basic types of tissues in the body, along with connective tissue, muscle tissue, and nervous tissue.
 
• They cover the body surfaces, line body cavities, and form glands.
 
• Epithelial tissues are classified based on the number of layers (simple or stratified) and the shape of the cells (squamous, cuboidal, or columnar).
 
 
 
• **Keratin**
 
 
• Keratin is a type of protein found in the skin, hair, and nails.
 
• It provides structural strength and helps protect cells from damage or stress.
 
 
 
• **Oesophagus**
 
 
• The oesophagus is a muscular tube that connects the throat (pharynx) with the stomach.
 
• It is lined with non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which provides protection from abrasion due to food passage.
 
 
 
• **Skin Layers**
 
 
• The skin is composed of three main layers: the epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis.
 
• The epidermis is the outermost layer, primarily made up of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
 
• The dermis lies beneath the epidermis and contains connective tissue, blood vessels, and nerve endings.
 
• The hypodermis, also known as the subcutaneous layer, contains fat and connective tissue that insulates and cushions the body.

questions.question: Pipe A is 3 times faster than pipe B. Both pipes together fill a tank in 36 min. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A is 3 times faster than pipe B. Both pipes together fill a tank in 36 min.

**Formula used:**

Let the time taken by pipe B alone to fill the tank be B minutes.

Then, time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank = B/3 minutes.

If both pipes together fill the tank in 36 minutes, then their combined rate is 1 tank per 36 minutes.

**Calculations:**

Rate of pipe B = 1/B tanks per minute

Rate of pipe A = 1/(B/3) = 3/B tanks per minute

Combined rate = 1/36 tanks per minute

⇒ 1/B + 3/B = 1/36

⇒ (1 + 3)/B = 1/36

⇒ 4/B = 1/36

⇒ B = 4 × 36 = 144 minutes

Time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank = B/3

⇒ Time taken by pipe A alone = 144/3 = 48 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: PQRS is a trapezium in which QR || PS and PR = RS. If ∠PQR = 96° and ∠QPR = 34°, then what is the measure of ∠PRS?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

PQRS is a trapezium in which QR || PS and PR = RS.

∠PQR = 96º

∠QPR = 34º

**Formula used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180º

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69be31d23c5617bc815032d0f4b6523c2a1ea4d7862710532c94ae57075eebd2.png] 

In triangle PQR:

∠PQR + ∠QPR + ∠PRQ = 180º

⇒ 96º + 34º + ∠PRQ = 180º

⇒ ∠PRQ = 50º

As, QR || PS so, ∠PRQ = ∠RPS = 50º

Since PR = RS, triangle PRS is isosceles.

Thus, ∠RPS = ∠RSP 

In triangle PRS:

∠PRS + 2 × ∠RPS = 180º

⇒ ∠PRS + 2 × 50º = 180º

⇒ ∠PRS = 180º - 100º

⇒ ∠PRS = 80º

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: The carbohydrates which are not used immediately are stored in the form of ________, which serves as the internal energy reserve to be used as and when required by the plant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**starch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants store carbohydrates in the form of starch, which is a **polysaccharide**.
 
• Starch consists of two types of molecules: **amylose (linear) and amylopectin (branched)**.
 
• It serves as an internal energy reserve for plants, used during periods of low photosynthetic activity.
 
• **Starch is stored in plastids**, such as chloroplasts and amyloplasts, within plant cells.
 
• When energy is required, starch is broken down into glucose by enzymatic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellulose**

 
 
• Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide and a major component of the plant cell wall.
 
• It is composed of linear chains of glucose molecules linked by** β-1,4-glycosidic bonds**.
 
• Unlike starch, cellulose cannot be digested by humans but can be broken down by some herbivores and microorganisms.
 
 
 
• **Glucose**
 
 
• **Glucose is a simple monosaccharide sugar** that serves as a primary energy source for cells.
 
• It is directly used in cellular respiration to produce ATP.
 
• Excess glucose can be converted into starch for storage in plants.
 
 
 
• **Glycogen**
 
 
• Glycogen is a storage form of glucose in animals and fungi, similar to starch in plants.
 
• It is highly branched and stored mainly in the liver and muscle tissues.
 
• Glycogen is broken down into glucose when energy is needed by the body.

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is present in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves and the hard covering of seeds and nuts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a type of **supportive tissue in plants**, characterized by thickened, lignified cell walls.
 
• It is present in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves, and the hard covering of seeds and nuts, providing structural support and strength.
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are typically** dead at maturity and provide rigidity and support to the plant**.
 
• This tissue is further divided into two types: **fibers** and **sclereids**, both contributing to the plant's mechanical strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apical Meristem**

 
 
• It is a tissue found at the **tips of roots and shoots**, responsible for the primary growth of the plant.
 
• Cells in the apical meristem are undifferentiated and actively divide to allow the plant to grow in length.
 
 
 
• **Epidermis**
 
 
• It is the **outermost layer of cells covering the leaves, flowers, roots, and stems of plants**.
 
• The epidermis serves as a protective barrier against environmental stress and pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma**
 
 
• This tissue is composed of living cells that are often involved in** storage, photosynthesis, and tissue repair**.
 
• Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls and are found throughout the plant.
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma**
 
 
• It is a type of plant tissue that **provides support to growing parts of the plant**, such as young stems and leaves.
 
• Collenchyma cells have unevenly thickened cell walls and are typically living at maturity.

__
 
• Equation (C), (v-u)=at, is derived from the basic definition of acceleration: acceleration (a) is the rate of change of velocity with time (t).
 
• This equation applies directly to uniformly accelerated motion, such as that of a freely falling object under gravity.
 
• It relates the final velocity (v) of an object to its initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and the time of travel (t).
 
• Equations (A) and (B) are not correctly written or applicable in the context of a freely falling object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• There are three primary equations of motion that describe the behavior of objects in uniformly accelerated linear motion:
 
 
• v=u+at
 
• s=ut+(1)/(2)at²
 
• v²=u²+2as
 
 
 
• These equations are essential in classical mechanics and are used to predict future motion based on current conditions.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:**
 
 
• Uniform acceleration refers to a constant acceleration, meaning the velocity of the object changes at a constant rate.
 
• In the case of free fall, the acceleration due to gravity (g) is approximately 9.81 m/s² near the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• Free fall is the motion of an object under the influence of gravitational force only.
 
• During free fall, the only force acting on the object is gravity, leading to a uniform acceleration downwards.

• These are plant hormones that promote stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering.
 
• They work by breaking seed dormancy and aiding in the mobilization of nutrients during seed germination.
 
 
 
• **Auxins**

questions.question: According to the Bohr's model, what is the maximum number of electrons for the second energy level?
questions.solution:

__
 
• According to the Bohr model, the second energy level can hold a maximum of **8 electrons**.
 
• Electrons in an atom are arranged in energy levels or shells, which are denoted by the principal quantum number (n).
 
• The formula to determine the maximum number of electrons in a shell is given by **2n²**, where n is the principal quantum number.
 
• For the second energy level (n=2), the maximum number of electrons is calculated as 2(2)² = 8.
 
• This concept is foundational to understanding the electron configuration of atoms and their chemical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Principal Quantum Number (n)**

 
 
• It denotes the **energy level** of an electron within an atom.
 
• The value of n determines the size and energy of the orbital.
 
• Higher values of n correspond to higher energy levels and larger orbitals.
 
 
 
• **Bohr Model**
 
 
• Proposed by** Niels Bohr in 1913**, it describes **electrons orbiting the nucleus in fixed energy levels**.
 
• Electrons can jump between energy levels by absorbing or emitting specific amounts of energy.
 
• The model helped explain the spectral lines of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Electron Configuration**
 
 
• It describes the distribution of electrons in the different energy levels or orbitals of an atom.
 
• It follows a s**pecific order based on the Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, and Hund's rule**.
 
• Electron configuration helps predict chemical behavior and bonding.
 
 
 
• **Aufbau Principle**
 
 
• It states that **electrons fill lower energy orbitals first** before moving to higher energy orbitals.
 
• This principle guides the order in which atomic orbitals are filled.

questions.question: A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken to fill half the tank by 1 tap = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 hours.

The remaining half of the tank is filled by 4 identical taps (1 original + 3 new).

Time taken by 4 taps to fill the remaining half = Time taken by 1 tap ÷ 4 = 3 ÷ 4 hours = 45 minutes.

Total time = 3 hours + 45 minutes = 3 hours 45 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours 45 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 

 **Tap**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 1 Tap
 6

 4 Taps
 1.5

⇒ Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM = 6 units.

⇒ Efficiency of 1 tap = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Time taken by 1 tap to fill half the tank (3 units) = 3 ÷ 1 = 3 hours.

⇒ Remaining work to be done = 6 − 3 = 3 units.

⇒ Now, 3 more similar taps are opened. Total taps operating = 1 + 3 = 4 taps.

⇒ Combined efficiency of 4 taps = 4 × 1 = 4 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken to complete the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency = 3 ÷ 4 hours.

⇒ Converting into minutes = (3 ÷ 4) × 60 = 45 minutes.

⇒ Total time taken to fill the tank completely = 3 hours + 45 minutes = 3 hours 45 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours 45 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Net Work

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in y hours, their combined 1 hour work is (1/x + 1/y).

Efficiency of Multiple Identical Sources

When n identical taps are opened simultaneously, their combined efficiency becomes n times the efficiency of a single tap, effectively reducing the time required to 1/n.

Work Equivalence

Total Work = Number of identical workers (or taps) × Time taken × Efficiency. This is a direct application of the unitary method in Time & Work.

questions.question: The term _______ refers to the densely packed kidney filtration unit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glomerulus**__.

__
 
• The glomerulus is a network of capillaries located at the beginning of a nephron in the kidney.
 
• It is involved in the filtration of blood to form urine.
 
• The glomerulus allows the passage of water, ions, and small molecules from the blood into the Bowman's capsule.
 
• It retains large molecules like proteins and blood cells within the bloodstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nephron**

 
 
• The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney responsible for urine formation.
 
• Each nephron includes a glomerulus and a renal tubule.
 
• There are approximately 1 million nephrons in each human kidney.
 
• The nephron performs essential functions like filtration, reabsorption, secretion, and excretion.
 
 
 
• **Bowman's Capsule**
 
 
• The Bowman's capsule is a cup-like sac that encases the glomerulus.
 
• It collects the filtrate that emerges from the glomerulus.
 
• This structure initiates the process of filtering blood to form urine.
 
 
 
• **Renal Tubule**
 
 
• The renal tubule processes the filtrate from the Bowman's capsule.
 
• It includes segments like the proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, and collecting duct.
 
• Each segment plays a specific role in reabsorbing water and solutes or secreting substances into the filtrate.
 
 
 
• **Filtration Barrier**
 
 
• The filtration barrier in the glomerulus consists of three layers: endothelial cells, basement membrane, and podocytes.
 
• It selectively allows the passage of small molecules while preventing large molecules like proteins from passing through.
 
• This barrier is crucial for maintaining the composition of blood and filtrate.

questions.question: An organism simply splits into two equal halves during cell division. What is it known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a type of asexual reproduction common among prokaryotes such as bacteria.
 
• In binary fission, an organism duplicates its genetic material and then divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.
 
• This process ensures that each daughter cell receives a copy of the parent organism's genetic material.
 
• Binary fission is efficient and allows for rapid population growth, especially in favorable environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regeneration**

 
 
• Regeneration is the process by which certain organisms can regrow lost or damaged parts of their body.
 
• Examples include the regrowth of limbs in starfish or tails in lizards.
 
• This is different from binary fission as it involves repairing or replacing damaged structures rather than creating new organisms.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• Budding is another form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• It is commonly observed in yeast and some invertebrates like hydra.
 
• Unlike binary fission, budding results in the formation of a new organism while the parent organism remains.
 
 
 
• **Spore formation**
 
 
• Spore formation is a method of asexual reproduction that involves the formation of spores by the parent organism.
 
• These spores are typically resistant to extreme conditions and can remain dormant for long periods.
 
• When conditions become favorable, spores germinate to form new organisms.
 
• This is a common reproductive strategy among fungi and some bacteria.

• The endoneurium surrounds individual nerve fibers, the perineurium surrounds bundles of nerve fibers (fascicles), and the epineurium surrounds the entire nerve.
 
• This hierarchical organization of connective tissue ensures that nerves are protected and can function effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Connective Tissue:**

 
 
• Loose connective tissue: Includes areolar, adipose, and reticular tissues.
 
• Dense connective tissue: Includes dense regular, dense irregular, and elastic tissues.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Connective Tissue:**
 
 
• Provides structural support to organs and tissues.
 
• Protects and insulates internal organs.
 
• Stores energy reserves, particularly in the form of fat.
 
• Transports substances within the body, particularly through blood, which is a type of connective tissue.
 
 
 
• **Nerve Structure:**

• Neurons are surrounded by myelin sheaths, which are produced by Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Connective Tissue Disorders:**
 
 
• Examples include Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Marfan syndrome, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
 
• These disorders can affect the integrity and function of connective tissues, leading to a variety of symptoms and complications.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the example/s of double displacement reaction?

(1) C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g)

(2) Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄ (s) + ₂NaCl(aq)

(3) Pb(s) + CuCl₂(aq) → PbCl₂(aq) + Cu(s)

(4) CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g)
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Double displacement reactions involve the exchange of ions between two compounds to form new compounds.
 
• In the reaction **Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) → BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)**, the sulfate (SO4²⁻) and chloride (Cl⁻) ions are displaced and form new products.
 
• This type of reaction typically produces a precipitate, a gas, or water.
 
• Double displacement reactions are also known as metathesis reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Single Displacement Reactions**

 
 
• Involve one element being replaced by another in a compound.
 
• Example: Pb(s) + CuCl2(aq) → PbCl2(aq) + Cu(s).
 
 
 
• **Combination Reactions**
 
 
• Two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• Example: C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g).
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reactions**
 
 
• A single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Example: CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g).
 
 
 
• **Precipitation Reactions**
 
 
• A type of double displacement reaction where an insoluble solid (precipitate) forms.
 
• Example: Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) → BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq).

• Michael Faraday discovered the principle of electromagnetic induction in 1831.
 
• Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction states that an electromotive force is induced in a conductor when there is a change in the magnetic field around it.

• **Lenz's Law:**
 
 
• Formulated by Heinrich Lenz in 1834, it states that the direction of the induced current will be such that it opposes the change in the magnetic field that produced it.

• It continues in the stomach where gastric juices break down proteins and fats.
 
• The small intestine is where most nutrient absorption occurs with the help of enzymes produced by the pancreas and bile from the liver.
 
• Indigestible substances are passed into the large intestine where water is absorbed, and the remaining material is excreted as feces.
 
 
 
• **Fossil Fuels**
 
 
• Fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas are formed over millions of years from the remains of plants and animals.
 
• They are used primarily for energy production but are harmful to the environment due to greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Biodegradation**
 
 
• Biodegradation is the process by which organic substances are broken down by living organisms, typically bacteria.

• **Human Health**
 
 
• Ingesting non-food substances can cause choking, poisoning, or internal injury.
 
• Medical attention should be sought immediately if non-food items are ingested.

questions.question:
Which of the following points always lie(s) on the principal axis of a spherical mirror?

i)Principal Focus

ii)Point of incidence

iii)Pole
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Principal Focus** of a spherical mirror is a point on the principal axis where light rays parallel to the principal axis converge (in concave mirrors) or appear to diverge from (in convex mirrors).
 
• The **Pole** of a spherical mirror is the midpoint of the mirror's surface, lying on the principal axis.
 
• Both the principal focus and the pole always lie on the principal axis of a spherical mirror.
 
• The **Point of incidence** is the point where the light ray strikes the mirror, which does not necessarily lie on the principal axis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spherical Mirror**

 
 
• A spherical mirror is a mirror that has the shape of a piece cut out of a spherical surface. There are two types: concave and convex mirrors.
 
• Concave mirrors converge light rays, while convex mirrors diverge them.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis**
 
 
• The principal axis is an imaginary line that passes through the pole and the center of curvature of the spherical mirror.
 
• It is the reference line for defining various properties and points related to the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature**
 
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere from which the spherical mirror is a part.
 
• It lies on the principal axis, at a distance equal to the radius of curvature from the pole.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the radius of the sphere from which the mirror is a part.
 
• It is twice the focal length in a spherical mirror.

Alkene, alkyne, and alkane hydrocarbons, respectively

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkyne, alkene, and alkane hydrocarbons, respectively**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **C2H2** is known as acetylene and is classified as an **alkyne hydrocarbon**.
 
• **C2H4** is known as ethylene and is classified as an **alkene hydrocarbon**.
 
• **C2H6** is known as ethane and is classified as an **alkane hydrocarbon**.
 
• Alkynes have a triple bond between carbon atoms, alkenes have a double bond, and alkanes have single bonds only.
 
• These classifications are based on the type of carbon-carbon bonds present in the molecule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrocarbon Types:**

 
 
• **Alkanes:** Saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds between carbon atoms (e.g., methane, ethane).
 
• **Alkenes:** Unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one double bond between carbon atoms (e.g., ethylene, propylene).
 
• **Alkynes:** Unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one triple bond between carbon atoms (e.g., acetylene, propyne).
 
 
 
• **Bond Characteristics:**
 
 
• Single bonds (sigma bonds) allow for free rotation around the bond axis.
 
• Double bonds (one sigma and one pi bond) restrict rotation and create a planar structure.
 
• Triple bonds (one sigma and two pi bonds) are linear and the shortest and strongest among the three types.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Alkanes are primarily used as fuels and lubricants.
 
• Alkenes are used in the production of polymers and as intermediates in chemical reactions.
 
• Alkynes are used in welding and as precursors to other chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism:**
 
 
• Hydrocarbons can exhibit structural isomerism, where compounds have the same molecular formula but different structures.
 
• Geometric isomerism is seen in alkenes due to the restricted rotation around the double bond.

questions.question: Modes of reproduction in various organisms depend on the
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mode of reproduction in organisms is significantly influenced by their **body structure and design**.
 
• Organisms with simpler body designs, such as single-celled organisms, typically reproduce asexually through processes like binary fission or budding.
 
• More complex organisms, including most animals and plants, often reproduce sexually, involving specialized reproductive organs and processes.
 
• The body design can determine the feasibility and efficiency of different reproductive strategies, ensuring the survival and adaptation of species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• Involves a single parent and produces offspring identical to the parent.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, and spore formation.
 
• Examples include bacteria (binary fission) and yeast (budding).
 
 
 
• **Sexual Reproduction**
 
 
• Involves the combination of genetic material from two parents to produce genetically diverse offspring.
 
• Involves specialized reproductive cells called gametes (sperm and egg).
 
• Common in animals, plants, and many other organisms.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Strategies**
 
 
• Reproductive strategies can be influenced by environmental factors, availability of mates, and evolutionary pressures.
 
• Some organisms can switch between asexual and sexual reproduction based on environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation and Survival**
 
 
• Reproductive modes are crucial for the adaptation and survival of species in changing environments.
 
• Genetic diversity from sexual reproduction can enhance the resilience of populations to diseases and environmental changes.

__
 
• The mass by mass percentage of a solution is calculated by dividing the mass of the solute by the mass of the solution and then multiplying by 100.
 
• This formula is used to express the concentration of a solution, indicating the amount of solute present in a given mass of the solution.
 
• The mass of the solution is the total mass of both the solute and the solvent combined.
 
• Mass by mass percentage is often used in chemistry and industry to prepare solutions with precise concentrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solution:**

• In a solution, the solute is uniformly distributed within the solvent.
 
 
 
• **Solute:**
 
 
• The substance that is dissolved in a solution.
 
• For example, in a saltwater solution, salt is the solute.
 
 
 
• **Solvent:**
 
 
• The substance that dissolves the solute to form a solution.
 
• Water is known as the "universal solvent" because it can dissolve many substances.
 
 
 
• **Concentration:**
 
 
• The amount of a substance (solute) present in a certain volume or mass of the solution or solvent.

questions.question: Which of the following terms defines the ability of metals to be drawn into thin wires?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ductility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ductility** is the property of a material that allows it to be drawn into thin wires.
 
• This property is most commonly observed in metals such as gold, silver, copper, and aluminum.
 
• **Gold** is known to be one of the most ductile metals, capable of being drawn into very fine wires.
 
• The measure of ductility is typically expressed as a percentage of elongation or the reduction of area in a tensile test.
 
• Ductility is essential for manufacturing processes like wire drawing and tube making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malleability**

 
 
• Malleability is the ability of a material to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without breaking.
 
• Like ductility, malleability is a property of metals, allowing them to be shaped and formed.
 
• Gold and silver are also highly malleable, making them useful for various industrial and jewelry applications.
 
 
 
• **Tensile Strength**
 
 
• Tensile strength is the maximum amount of tensile stress that a material can withstand before failure.
 
• It is an important property for materials that are used in structures and machines.
 
• High tensile strength materials are often also ductile, but this is not always the case.
 
 
 
• **Brittleness**
 
 
• Brittleness is the tendency of a material to break or shatter without significant deformation when under stress.
 
• Brittle materials, like glass, ceramics, and some polymers, have low ductility and malleability.
 
• These materials are often used where high hardness and low deformability are required.
 
 
 
• **Plasticity**
 
 
• Plasticity is the ability of a material to undergo permanent deformation without breaking.
 
• This property is crucial for processes such as forging, molding, and stamping.
 
• Metals and polymers typically exhibit high plasticity.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following options.

options.text: The kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its position.

The kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
The kinetic energy of an object increases with the increase of its velocity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The kinetic energy of an object is the energy it possesses due to its motion, not its position.
 
• Kinetic energy increases with the mass of the object; the formula is KE = 0.5 * m * v², where m is mass and v is velocity.
 
• Kinetic energy also increases with the square of the object's velocity.
 
• Potential energy, not kinetic energy, is related to the position of an object in a force field, such as gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)**

 
 
• Defined as the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• The SI unit of kinetic energy is the Joule (J).
 
• Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity; it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• Examples of kinetic energy include a moving car, a flying airplane, and flowing water.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy (PE)**
 
 
• Energy possessed by an object due to its position or state.
 
• Examples include gravitational potential energy, elastic potential energy, and chemical potential energy.
 
• Potential energy can be converted into kinetic energy and vice versa.
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**
 
 
• The work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• Mathematically, W = ΔKE, where W is work done and ΔKE is the change in kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy**
 
 
• States that energy cannot be created or destroyed but can only be transformed from one form to another.
 
• In a closed system, the total energy remains constant.

questions.question: The focal length of a spherical mirror is 12 cm, then the radius of curvature of this mirror will be:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The radius of curvature (R) of a spherical mirror is twice the focal length (f).
 
• Given the focal length (f) is 12 cm, the formula R = 2f can be applied.
 
• By substituting f = 12 cm into the formula, we get R = 2 * 12 cm.
 
• Thus, the radius of curvature (R) is 24 cm.
 
• This relationship holds true for both concave and convex mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spherical Mirrors:**

 
 
• Spherical mirrors are mirrors with a consistent curvature, such as concave and convex mirrors.
 
• Concave mirrors curve inward, focusing light to a point, and are used in applications like telescopes.
 
• Convex mirrors curve outward, spreading light out, and are used for wide-angle viewing like in vehicle side mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The focal length is the distance between the mirror's surface and its focal point, where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge.
 
• In concave mirrors, the focal point is in front of the mirror; in convex mirrors, it is behind the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the radius of the sphere from which the spherical mirror is a segment.
 
• The center of this sphere is called the center of curvature, and the radius connects it to any point on the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Equation:**
 
 
• The mirror equation relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and the focal length (f): 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.
 
• This equation is essential for understanding image formation by spherical mirrors.

questions.question: If an object with a mass of 0.1 kg moves with a uniform velocity of 2 ms⁻¹, its kinetic energy is

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• The formula for calculating kinetic energy (KE) is: K.E=(1)/(2)mv²
 
• In this problem, the mass (m) of the object is **0.1 kg**.
 
• The velocity (v) of the object is **2 m/s**.
 
• Using the formula:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy:**

 
 
• Energy is the capacity to do work and is measured in joules (J) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• Different forms of energy include kinetic energy, potential energy, thermal energy, chemical energy, and more.
 
 
 
• **Mass:**
 
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is measured in kilograms (kg) in the SI unit.
 
• It is an intrinsic property of an object and does not change with its location.
 
 
 
• **Velocity:**
 
 
• Velocity is the speed of an object in a specific direction and is measured in meters per second (m/s) in the SI unit.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
 
 
• **Work:**
 
 
• Work is done when a force applied to an object moves it through a distance.
 
• It is calculated as the product of the force and the distance moved in the direction of the force, measured in joules (J).

questions.question: To move an object on a horizontal table, one needs to apply:

options.text: an equal amount of perpendicular forces on the object in both upward and downward directions
only a single force perpendicular to the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**unbalanced force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An unbalanced force is necessary to change the state of motion of an object, as per Newton's First Law of Motion.
 
• Applying an unbalanced force to an object on a horizontal table overcomes the frictional force between the object and the table surface.
 
• When the forces acting on an object are unbalanced, they cause a change in the object's velocity, resulting in acceleration.
 
• The direction of the unbalanced force determines the direction in which the object will move.
 
• An unbalanced force implies that the net force acting on the object is not zero, leading to motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia)**

 
 
• States that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
 
• Highlights the concept of inertia, which is the tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion.
 
 
 
• **Friction**
 
 
• A force that opposes the relative motion or tendency of such motion of two surfaces in contact.
 
• Can be reduced by applying lubricants or by using smoother surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Balanced Forces**
 
 
• When two forces acting on an object are equal in size but opposite in direction, they are balanced forces.
 
• Balanced forces do not cause a change in the motion of an object.
 
 
 
• **Net Force**
 
 
• The overall force acting on an object when all the individual forces acting on it are combined.
 
• If the net force is not zero, the forces are unbalanced, leading to a change in the object's motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)** is a fuel gas mainly composed of **methane, compressed to less than 1% of its volume** at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)** consists mainly of **propane, butane, or a mixture of these gases**, and is stored in liquid form under moderate pressure.
 
• CNG is primarily used as an alternative to gasoline, diesel, and propane fuel in vehicles.
 
• LPG is commonly used for heating, cooking, and as a fuel for certain vehicles and equipment.
 
• Both CNG and LPG are considered cleaner alternatives to other fossil fuels, emitting lower levels of pollutants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methane (CH₄)**

 
 
• Methane is a colorless, odorless, and highly flammable gas, which is the main component of natural gas.
 
• It is used as a fuel and is a major greenhouse gas, contributing to global warming.
 
• CNG is primarily composed of methane, making it a cleaner burning fuel compared to gasoline and diesel.
 
 
 
• **Propane (C₃H₈)**
 
 
• Propane is a three-carbon alkane gas, normally compressed and stored as a liquid.
 
• It is widely used in heating, cooking, and as a fuel for engines.
 
• Propane is a major component of LPG.
 
 
 
• **Butane (C₄H₁₀)**
 
 
• Butane is a four-carbon alkane gas, usually found mixed with propane in LPG.
 
• It is used in lighters, portable stoves, and as a propellant in aerosol sprays.
 
• Butane is another key component of LPG.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• CNG vehicles produce lower emissions of carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter compared to gasoline and diesel vehicles.
 
• LPG burns more cleanly than many other fossil fuels, resulting in fewer greenhouse gases and pollutants.
 
• Both CNG and LPG contribute to reducing the carbon footprint when used as alternative fuels.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about a mixture and determine which of the statements is/are correct.

1. A mixture has a variable composition.

2. In compounds, the composition of each new substance is always fixed.

3. A mixture shows the properties of the constituent substances.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A mixture has a variable composition, meaning the proportions of its components can vary.
 
• In compounds, the composition of each new substance is always fixed, with elements combined in definite ratios.
 
• A mixture exhibits the properties of the substances that make it up, without chemical bonding between the components.
 
• Mixtures can be separated into their individual components by physical means such as filtration, distillation, or evaporation.
 
• Examples of mixtures include air, which is a mixture of gases, and saltwater, which is a mixture of salt and water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures**

 
 
• These mixtures have a uniform composition throughout. Examples include solutions like sugar in water.
 
• The different components of a homogeneous mixture cannot be easily distinguished.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixtures**
 
 
• These mixtures have a non-uniform composition. Examples include mixtures like sand in water.
 
• The different components of a heterogeneous mixture can be easily distinguished.
 
 
 
• **Physical Separation Techniques**
 
 
• Filtration: Used to separate solids from liquids in a heterogeneous mixture.
 
• Distillation: Used to separate liquids based on differences in boiling points.
 
• Evaporation: Used to separate a dissolved solid from a liquid.
 
 
 
• **Compounds vs. Mixtures**
 
 
• Compounds are substances formed when two or more elements are chemically bonded together, with fixed composition.
 
• Mixtures involve physical blending of two or more substances without chemical bonding.

questions.question: A retailer permits a trade discount of 15%, followed by a cash discount of 20%, on an article. The net percentage of discount is :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A retailer permits a trade discount of 15%, followed by a cash discount of 20%, on an article.

**Calculation:**

Let the original price be 100.

After a trade discount of 15%, the price becomes:

⇒ 100 - 15% of 100 = 100 - 15 = 85

After a cash discount of 20%, the price becomes:

⇒ 85 - 20% of 85 = 85 - 17 = 68

Therefore, the net discount is:

⇒ 100 - 68 = 32

⇒ Net percentage discount = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question:
An object weighs 60 N when measured on the Earth. What would be its weight when measured on the moon?

(Given, acceleration due to gravity (g) of the moon is 1/6 th of the g of the earth)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The weight of an object depends on the gravitational force acting on it, which varies from planet to planet.
 
• On the Earth, the object weighs 60 N due to Earth's gravitational acceleration (g ≈ 9.81 m/s²).
 
• The Moon's gravitational acceleration is approximately 1/6th that of Earth's (g ≈ 1.63 m/s²).
 
• Weight on the Moon is calculated by dividing the Earth's weight by 6 (60 N ÷ 6 = 10 N).
 
• Therefore, the object would weigh 10 N on the Moon.

• It is the force that attracts a body towards the center of the Earth or any other celestial body.
 
• The gravitational force on the Moon is about 1/6th of that on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:**
 
 
• Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object (measured in Newtons).
 
• Mass is the amount of matter in an object (measured in kilograms) and remains constant regardless of location.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**
 
 
• It states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• On the Moon, the acceleration due to gravity is less, hence the weight is less for the same mass.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Significance:**
 
 
• Understanding weight differences on different celestial bodies is crucial for space exploration and missions.
 
• Astronauts need to adjust for these differences during lunar missions.

questions.question: Which of the following transports food, carbon dioxide and nitrogenous wastes in a dissolved form?

The correct answer is __**Plasma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasma** is the liquid component of blood that transports nutrients, hormones, and proteins to the parts of the body that need it.
 
• It makes up about **55% of the body's total blood volume**.
 
• Plasma carries carbon dioxide, which is a waste product of cellular metabolism, from tissues to the lungs for exhalation.
 
• It also transports nitrogenous wastes to the kidneys for excretion.
 
• Plasma helps maintain blood pressure and regulates body temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood Composition**

 
 
• Blood consists of cells suspended in plasma: red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets.
 
• RBCs are responsible for oxygen transport, WBCs are involved in immune response, and platelets play a key role in blood clotting.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Plasma**
 
 
• Plasma serves as a medium for transporting nutrients, waste products, and other substances throughout the body.
 
• It contains clotting factors that help prevent excessive bleeding during injury.
 
• Plasma proteins, like albumin, help maintain osmotic balance and transport hormones, vitamins, and drugs.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide Transport**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is primarily transported in the blood in the form of bicarbonate ions (HCO3-).
 
• A smaller amount is dissolved directly in plasma, and some bind to hemoglobin in red blood cells.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogenous Wastes**
 
 
• Nitrogenous wastes like urea and creatinine are byproducts of protein metabolism.
 
• These wastes are carried by plasma to the kidneys, where they are filtered out and excreted in urine.

questions.question: Silver ornaments become black after some time because silver reacts with ______ present in the air.
questions.solution:

__
 
• Silver ornaments tarnish and turn black due to the formation of silver sulphide (Ag₂S).
 
• This reaction occurs when silver comes into contact with hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) present in the air.
 
• The chemical reaction is:** 4Ag + 2H₂S + O₂ → 2Ag₂S + 2H₂O**.
 
• Hydrogen sulphide is often found in polluted air, emitted from sources like sewage, swamps, and industrial processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silver Tarnishing**

 
 
• Tarnishing is a surface discoloration on silver, a result of the metal reacting with sulphur compounds in the air.
 
• Tarnish is essentially corrosion that affects only the outer layers of the metal.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S)**
 
 
• It is a colorless gas with a characteristic odor of rotten eggs.
 
• It is produced naturally by the decomposition of organic matter and is also a by-product of industrial activities.
 
 
 
• **Preventing Tarnish**
 
 
• Storing silver in airtight containers can reduce exposure to air and pollutants.
 
• Using anti-tarnish strips or bags can also help in preventing tarnish.
 
 
 
• **Cleansing Tarnished Silver**
 
 
• Tarnished silver can be cleaned using silver polish or homemade remedies like baking soda and vinegar.
 
• A common method involves placing silver in aluminum foil and soaking it in a solution of baking soda and hot water.
